meta_title: TigerTag Firebase Integration: connect your own client
meta_description: Reference for Home Assistant, ESP32, Python and Spoolman clients that read and update TigerTag filament spools through Firebase Auth and Firestore.
og_description: Sign in with the user's own TigerTag account, read their spools, update weights: the reference for third-party clients, with examples.
og_alt: TigerTag Firebase Integration: the reference for Home Assistant, ESP32, Python and Spoolman clients
hero_headline: Connect Home Assistant, an ESP32 scale or a Python script to a TigerTag account.
hero_lead: This repository documents how any client signs in with the user's own TigerTag credentials, reads their filament spools and racks in Firestore, and writes spool weights back. What is documented here is what is deployed, and every change to it is recorded in the changelog.
flow_alt: How a client connects: the client signs in to Firebase Authentication with the user's email and password, sends the returned idToken to Firestore, and Firestore Security Rules decide what it may read or write in users/{uid}/inventory.
flow_auth: The user's own account, a 1-hour idToken
flow_rules: Owners read and write, friends read
fact2_label: Lifetime of an idToken: refresh it before it expires
fact4_label: Minimum deprecation notice before a field is renamed or removed
how_title: How a client connects to TigerTag
how_lead: Every client follows the same four steps: fetch the public Firebase config, sign in as the user, call the Firestore REST API with the user's token, and keep that token fresh.
step1_text: One GET returns the Firebase project config. The apiKey is public by design: it identifies the project, not the caller. Cache it; a weekly refresh is enough.
step2_text: The user's own email and password return a UID, a 1-hour idToken and a refreshToken. Google Sign-In needs a browser, so headless clients use a password.
step3_text: Send the idToken as a Bearer token. Spools live in users/{uid}/inventory, racks in users/{uid}/racks; weights are net grams, dates Unix milliseconds.
step4_text: Refresh the idToken before the hour is up and replace both stored tokens. On a permission-denied, refresh once and retry the read once.
how_code_title: The three calls, from the documentation
how_code_note: The values in braces come from the previous call: apiKey and projectId from the config, uid and idToken from the sign-in.
int_lead: Each guide in docs/clients covers authentication, the data it reads or writes, the field mapping and the code. The snippets below are copied from the guides.
ha_text: A Home Assistant custom component that exposes one sensor per spool, with the remaining weight in grams as its state. The guide also covers friends' inventories, pagination and token storage; the config flow and sensor are skeletons, and a fully runnable component is still to be written.
esp_text: For a scale or NFC device: look up a spool by the scanned RFID UID (uid, then twin_uid), compute the net weight and write weight_available and last_update with an update mask. The guide ends with a complete ESP32 sketch (WiFi, ArduinoJson).
py_text: A minimal Python client built on Pyrebase4: it signs in, lists your spools and prints how many spools each friend has. The guide holds the whole script and a sample run.
sm_text: A one-way bridge from TigerTag to a Spoolman instance: brands become vendors, each brand, material and colour becomes a filament, and each inventory document becomes a spool, upserted through Spoolman's REST API. Run it from cron, systemd or Docker.
scale_text: The contract a TigerScale or compatible scale follows to appear online in Tiger Studio Manager and the TigerTag mobile app: a heartbeat document every 30 seconds, a weight update on every stable reading, and twin tags written in one atomic batch.
int_note: Building for another platform? A new guide goes in docs/clients, an optional runnable example in examples/.
sec_title: The user's account, the user's rules
sec_lead: There is no shared key to protect and no master token to leak: a client can do exactly what its user can do, and Firestore enforces it on the server.
sec1_text: Every client signs in with the end user's own credentials. Never ship the firebase-admin SDK or any admin key in a third-party client.
sec2_text: Firestore Security Rules check every request against request.auth.uid: owners read and write their own documents, friends may read inventory and racks, and anything not allowed is denied. The public copy of the rules is in rules/firestore.rules.
sec3_text: Accepting a friend request writes a document on each side. While users/{friend}/friends/{you} exists you may read that friend's inventory and racks, read-only; deleting it cuts access immediately.
sec4_text: Poll every 5 minutes at most often, never under 30 seconds, write only when a value changes, and pass a limit on list reads (200 spools, 50 racks). Firebase App Check is not enforced.
contract_lead: The repository is treated as a public contract: changes that affect clients reach this repository in the same release, and the changelog records each one as Added, Changed, Deprecated, Removed, Fixed or Security.
stable1: Document paths such as users/{uid}/inventory/{spoolId}, users/{uid}/racks/{rackId} and users/{uid}/friends/{friendUid}.
stable2: The name and meaning of every documented field: weight_available is net grams, last_update is Unix milliseconds, deleted: true means soft-deleted.
stable3: The friend access model, and the Firebase Auth endpoints a client signs in with.
stable4: The apiKey and projectId, unless the whole project moves, announced at least 6 months ahead.
may1: Lookup tables gain new brands and materials; numeric ids are append-only and never reused.
may2: Convenience HTTPS endpoints at cdn.tigertag.io can evolve their request and response shapes.
may3: New collections and new fields are always additive: ignore the fields you do not know and stay compatible.
docs_lead: The core documents every integration builds on, in the order a client needs them.
doc1: The public Firebase config endpoint, what each field is for, and how long to cache it.
doc2: Email and password sign-in, token refresh, and the permission-denied retry pattern.
doc3: Every Firestore collection and field: inventory, racks, friends, profiles, scales.
doc4: How friend access works: public codes, private keys, the bidirectional bond.

eco_lead: This guide covers the cloud account. The chips, the apps and the SDKs have their own repositories.
eco_proto_text: The open NFC chip format for filament spools and resin bottles, its specification and the reference database.
eco_studio_text: The desktop app (Electron) that manages the same inventory; the documentation is verified against its releases.

faq1_q: Do I need a service account or an admin key?
faq1_a: No. Every client signs in with the end user's own TigerTag email and password, and Firestore Security Rules decide what that user may read or write. There is no shared admin key, and the firebase-admin SDK must never be used in a third-party client.
faq2_q: Why is the Firebase apiKey public?
faq2_a: The apiKey identifies the TigerTag Firebase project, not the caller. Without a valid idToken, obtained by signing in as a real user, it gives access to nothing; access control is done by authentication and by the Security Rules.
faq3_q: Can Home Assistant or an ESP32 sign in with Google?
faq3_a: Not directly: Google Sign-In needs a browser redirect. A user who has only ever used Google sets a password on the account first, through the desktop or mobile app's forgot-password flow, and then signs in with email and password.
faq4_q: How often may my integration poll?
faq4_a: Every 5 minutes at most often for a sensor, every 15 minutes for a rack overview, and never under 30 seconds. A scale writes only when a weight changes. List reads should pass a limit: 200 for inventory, 50 for racks.
faq5_q: Can my integration read a friend's spools?
faq5_a: Yes, read-only. When two users are friends, each has a document for the other under users/{uid}/friends, and the rules let a friend read the inventory and racks. Either user can remove the friendship at any time, which cuts access immediately.
faq6_q: What if production disagrees with this documentation?
faq6_a: The documentation wins: a difference means a regression shipped. Open an issue on the repository with the page, the path you read or wrote and the response, with tokens and private keys removed.
faq7_q: Under which licence can I reuse the code?
